item.title: Convicted murderer wants B.C. Supreme Court to throw out case over delays
item.description: VANCOUVER — A man convicted of first-degree murder in a killing police have said was linked to organized crime has asked British Columbia Supreme Court to throw out the case, arguing that delays in the process violated his Charter rights.

item.title: Central Africa Republic President Faustin Archange Touadéra reelected, provisional results show
item.description: BANGUI, Central Africa Republic (AP) — Central Africa Republic President Faustin Archange Touadéra won a third term in last month's election , provisional results showed.

item.title: B.C. Conservative MP Scott Anderson says he rejected Liberal approach to cross floor
item.description: VERNON — A British Columbia member of Parliament says he's been approached to cross the floor to give Mark Carney's Liberal government a majority, but he's not interested in "betraying" his constituents.

item.title: Quebec students must address teachers as 'Mr.' and 'Ms.' under new civility rules
item.description: MONTREAL — Quebec students returning to class after winter break will now have to use formal language to address their teachers under new rules designed to foster civility.

item.title: Quebec Liberals name ethics officer for leadership race after vote-buying allegations
item.description: MONTREAL — The Quebec Liberal Party has named an ethics officer to supervise the upcoming leadership race after allegations of wrongdoing sunk the previous leader.

item.title: Freeland steps down as Canada's Ukraine envoy, will resign as MP soon
item.description: OTTAWA — Liberal MP Chrystia Freeland said Monday she is stepping down as the prime minister's special representative for the reconstruction of Ukraine and will leave Parliament in the coming weeks — hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky

item.title: Experts say Canada should co-ordinate Western Hemisphere response to Maduro's ouster
item.description: OTTAWA — Foreign policy experts say Ottawa should reach out to nations threatened by the United States to co-ordinate a response to the Trump administration's ouster of Venezuela's autocratic ruler.

item.title: Carney arrives in Paris for talks with Ukraine's allies about security guarantees
item.description: PARIS — Prime Minister Mark Carney arrived in Paris Monday ahead of a meeting with Ukraine's allies to pursue security agreements to prevent Russia from repeating its invasion if a ceasefire deal is reached.

item.title: As Ontario civil servants return to office full time, union calls order 'ridiculous'
item.description: TORONTO — Ontario government employees are expected to return to the office five days per week starting Monday, despite objections from public sector unions.

item.title: 'Frostbite capital': Efforts to reduce frostbite amputations underway in Edmonton
item.description: EDMONTON — Trevor Logan winces in pain as a nurse cleans the blistered middle finger on his right hand, swollen to twice its size due to frostbite.
